description: We are a passionate team of six students bringing together coding, AI/ML, research, UI/UX, backend, frontend, and storytelling skills. Inspired by the challenges of human space exploration, we are building AURA-X, an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring and risk prediction prototype. We believe in learning together, solving real problems creatively, and turning space-data ideas into an engaging, meaningful solution for the future of human missions.
summary:
AURA-X is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring and risk prediction system designed for long-duration space missions.

The system continuously analyzes simulated physiological telemetry such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, sleep, recovery, workload, stress, and activity. AURA-X combines these signals into a dynamic health-risk score and classifies the astronaut's condition as LOW, MODERATE, ELEVATED, or CRITICAL.

The platform also provides a 6-hour health-risk forecast, AI-generated health recommendations, and a digital-twin model representing physiological adaptation across multiple body systems.

Our prototype is designed to demonstrate how autonomous health intelligence could support astronauts when communication with Earth is delayed or limited. The current prototype uses simulated data and is not a medical device.
details:
AURA-X is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring and risk prediction platform designed to support crew health during long-duration space missions. It combines simulated astronaut biometric telemetry, health indicators, radiation exposure data, and mission conditions into an interactive dashboard.

The system uses a FastAPI backend for data processing and API services, an AI/ML layer for health-risk prediction and analysis, and a React-based frontend for real-time visualization. The platform presents astronaut health trends, risk levels, alerts, and AI-generated explanations in a simple mission-control interface.

AURA-X is designed as a prototype using simulated astronaut data rather than real personal astronaut medical records. Its goal is to demonstrate how AI, data visualization, and mission-health monitoring could help crews and mission teams identify potential health risks early and make informed decisions.

The project combines software development, AI/ML, aerospace-health research, data analysis, UI/UX design, and interactive visualization into one unified solution.
